title: Eagle Eye Shields in Jacksonville and Alonzo Ross
summary: Hall writes Eagle Eye Shields for money, joins his band in Jacksonville, and is recruited by Alonzo Ross for Miami.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I'll tell you the story. After being in Pensacola, Florida, then we decided to make a tour of Florida. We went down to Jacksonville, Florida. So when we was in Jacksonville, Florida, I met a fellow there by the name of Eagle Eye Shields. So he liked what I was doing, so he asked me, he said, anytime you want to, anytime things get tough with you, you want to come down to Jacksonville. He had all to go down to Jacksonville anyway. He said, come on down, let me know, and we can get together. I'll put you in my band, okay? So, you know, we went back to Pensacola, Florida. I'll never forget, we was in Mobile, Alabama. We had a couple of days off. Things got a little tough. So I thought about this Eagle Eye Shields. So I wrote him a letter. And I told somebody in the band, I said, well, if this guy is me in business, I'm going to ask him for some money. So I asked him for $50. The next day I got the $50. So I said, well, this guy is me in business. So I went on down. He paid my way, train, fare and everything. So I went on down to Jacksonville, Florida. And I stayed with his band for, oh, quite a long time. Because he used to do all his own booking. There was no booking agent then, you know? So there was another fellow in Jacksonville, Florida, had a band by the name of Alonzo Ross. So he was working in Miami, Florida. But he was originally from Jacksonville and he heard me playing so he wanted me to play with his band now in Miami, Florida. So I told him, I said, so I'm a little ahead of my story. But anyway, by being in Jacksonville, Florida, so we wanted a trumpet player. If you remember, it was a, we were talking about a trumpet player just a while ago by the name of Anderson. He had all the go. He was working with Eagle Eye Shield then. At that time, this fellow by the name of Broadway Jones from New York used to go down to Miami, Florida. As a singer. So he decided he'd take a band to New York. So he took the trumpet player from Eagle Eye Shield's band. So he was stuck with trumpet player. So he asked me where could we get a trumpet player and I recommend Cootie, Cootie Williams. That's how Cootie Williams left Mobile, Alabama. So I got permission from his father, being a kid. So we had him to come down to Jacksonville. So he joined the band, see. So after Alonzo Ross wanted me to join his band, so I told him, I got a kid I got to look out for, which is Cootie Williams. So if you can make room for him, we'll join your band. So next couple of days, I got a letter from Ross, say, I'll make room for Cootie. So I said, well, this is it. So Cootie and I joined Alonzo Ross' band. So Alonzo Ross was making a tour of Florida, and so when he came through Jacksonville, we joined his band, so then, well, the only, I think he was working nine months out of a year down in Miami, Florida. So when he went down to Florida, next time to Miami, we went through. From there, Victor is scouting around for musician. You know what I mean, band. We had some original tune. So we were touring Georgia. And if you remember, it was a band by the name of Black Steel. Blue Steel. Blue Steel. Was it Blue Steel or Black Steel? Something like that. And if you remember years of one of the things, you remember that, that tune, Girl of My Dreams? Yeah. Well, it was written by one of the guys in that band. The Blue Steel? Yeah. And Victor wanted that particular tune. Well, he wouldn't sell it to him unless his band would record it. So they sent a portable set down to Savannah, Georgia, and they recorded the tune. And we was in Savannah, Georgia, and we had some original tune, so the next day we, Alonzo, a band, recorded for Victor. For, in the, so when the record came out, the guy at the Roseland Bar, I mean, he heard the record. He's looking for talent. So he sent for the band to come to New York. And that's how we got to New York. And I've been there ever since, 1928.
